newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy may levy tax to fund Albania mission-reports.
newsitem.headline: Italy may levy tax to fund Albania mission-reports.

text.p: Italy may have to levy a special tax to meet the cost of sending a military force on a humanitarian mission to Albania, Italian newspapers reported on Sunday.
Newspapers reported the cost of a three-month mission, which still has to win approval from parliament, would amount to 90 billion lire.

Piero Fassino, under secretary at the Foreign Ministry, was quoted by Milan daily Il Sole 24 Ore as saying that a special tax to fund the mission, part of a multinational security force, was a possibility.

An Italian mission to Bosnia in 1995 cost 200 billion lire and was financed with a special tax on lead-free petrol, while the sending of troops to Somalia and Mozambique in 1993 was partly funded by a tax on diesel oil.

"The peace mission in Albania will be financed, as has happened with missions to Mozambique, Bosnia by drawing in part on existing funds and in part on extraordinary funds. Generally in these cases additional taxes of various kinds have been used," said Fassino.
But he added that a tax is "only one of the hypotheses and not the (only) hypothesis."
